import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Map 'has_video_4k' to descriptive labels for better legend readability
df['has_video_4k_label'] = df['has_video_4k'].map({0: 'No 4K Video', 1: 'Has 4K Video'})

# Set a style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
ax = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',  # Color points by sensor type
    style='has_video_4k_label',  # Use different markers for 4K video capability
    s=100,  # Marker size
    alpha=0.7,  # Transparency of points
    palette='viridis',  # Color palette for hue
    edgecolor='w',  # White edge for markers for better separation
    linewidth=0.5,  # Line width of the edge
    legend=False  # Disable automatic legend generation to manually create and place them
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type and 4K Video Capability', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Manually create and place legends for better control
# Get handles and labels that would have been generated by seaborn
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()

# Determine the number of unique hue categories (sensor types)
num_hue_categories = len(df['sensor_type'].unique())

# Create the legend for 'Sensor Type'
hue_legend = ax.legend(handles[:num_hue_categories], labels[:num_hue_categories],
                       title='Sensor Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)
ax.add_artist(hue_legend)  # Add the first legend back to the axes

# Create the legend for '4K Video Capability'
style_legend = ax.legend(handles[num_hue_categories:], labels[num_hue_categories:],
                         title='4K Video Capability', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.7), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Ensure tight layout to prevent labels/legends from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
